title: HOSA Nutrition: Medical Nutrition Therapy - Nutrition - Medical Nutrition Therapy - GI
subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A client has recently been diagnosed with Celiac Disease. Which of the following lunch options is safe for them to consume?
options: Whole wheat wrap with grilled chicken
Quinoa salad with grilled salmon and olive oil dressing
questions.explain: Celiac disease requires a strictly Gluten-Free diet. Wheat, Barley, and Rye contain gluten. Quinoa is a naturally gluten-free grain.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with Diverticulosis asks for dietary advice to prevent complications. Which dietary modification is most appropriate?
options: Low fiber diet to rest the bowel
High fiber diet with adequate fluid intake
Avoidance of all seeds and nuts
questions.explain: For Diverticulosis (the asymptomatic condition), a high fiber diet is recommended to prevent constipation and diverticula formation. (Contrast with Diverticulitis, where low fiber is used during acute inflammation).
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is advised to follow a Low-FODMAP diet. Which of the following foods should be avoided during the elimination phase?
questions.explain: Onions and garlic are high in fructans (a type of FODMAP) and are common triggers for IBS symptoms. The other options are generally low-FODMAP.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) complains of heartburn at night. Which recommendation is most appropriate?
options: Avoid eating within 3 hours of bedtime.
Increase intake of chocolate and caffeine.
questions.explain: Eating close to bedtime increases the risk of reflux. Peppermint, chocolate, and lying down decrease lower esophageal sphincter (LES) pressure, worsening GERD.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with Cystic Fibrosis (CF) has malabsorption due to pancreatic insufficiency. What specific nutritional supplement is routinely required?
options: Pancreatic enzymes (PERT) with meals and snacks
questions.explain: CF blocks pancreatic ducts, preventing enzymes from reaching the intestine. PERT (Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy) is necessary to digest food.
